  Design decisions the implementer made and will report (judge them, do not take them as given):
  (1) D1 roots: a static root element owned by another static element has its root held by that owning static (A4, RootHeld in WF3), not by frame 0; D1 says 'une racine Modify par emplacement racine, détenue par le cadre 0'. Without this, WF3 fails on the initial state.
  (2) D3 entries keep the fields available and issued of the pass-4 Arena record besides storage and internal; D3 says entries are {storage, internal}.
  (3) D3 ArenaInv revised: 'storage is an owned root' becomes 'storage owned by a place' (OwnedStorage) and 'internal has no origin' is dropped, because D3 lets internal be a block of another arena.
  (4) newArena also requires OwnedStorage (A10: storage owned by the arena value); D3 lists three preconditions only. Claimed counterexample without it: arena on a part of a frame-owned local whose internal is a derived authority held by the frame, then passed as an enterFrame parameter, breaking ArenaInv.
  (5) newArena's internal is the first authority (lowest index) that is active, Modify, held by the owner of storage, with footprint exactly that of storage; newArena rejects if none.
  (6) arena_inv_preserved gains hypothesis (hlive : s'.Active ar.internal), needed at the exit when internal is a derived block.
  (7) The nested arena of the task case list (child arena value distinct from the parent's, 'ok après endUse de l'enfant et de son bloc') is claimed not representable: a block region is always storage owned by the parent arena value, while D3 asks internal held by the owner of the child storage; the only realisable nesting issues the block to the parent arena value itself. The module tests that variant (reset rejected while the child lives, accepted after release of the child's internal).
  (8) The case 'retour d'une valeur contenant un accès dérivé Modify' is realised with an arena block, since derive and split give the frame as holder.

  [
    {
      "title": "The nested-arena case of task §5 cannot be built as written. The module tests a different scenario (release instead of endUse), and D3 makes the child and parent arenas always share one arena value",
      "severity": "major",
      "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:8430-8470 (nA0..nA5, nested_reachable); interaction of D3 with WF3 at line 1557",
      "cause": "spec defect",
      "evidence": "Task §5 asks for a child arena on a block of the parent, with reset of the parent giving reject while the child lives and `ok après endUse de l'enfant et de son bloc`. D3 requires `internal` to be held by the owner of `storage`. WF3 (line 1557) forces a part to have its parent's owner (`pr.owner = pl.owner`). So the block region's place is always owned by the parent arena value, and newArena only succeeds when the block was issued to that same value. I checked this in Lean (scratchpad rev10/stmt/checks2.lean). In a fresh run, the parent issues block [4] to another Uninit local 2 (IssueAt ... (.ok nC4) builds), and then both `NewArenaStep 4 nC4 .reject` and `NewArenaStep 2 nC4 .reject` hold. In the module's own realisation, endUse of the child's arena value also ends the parent (checks.lean): `EndUseStep K0 0 nA5 (.ok (endUseEff nA5 0))`, `¬ (endUseEff nA5 0).Active 2` and `ResetAtStep K0 0 0 (endUseEff nA5 0) .reject` all build. The brief's expected `ok` after endUse therefore cannot be obtained. The module replaces it with `ReleaseStep 3 nA5` (line 8452) and then reset ok. This confirms implementer claim (7), but the case's verdict as specified is not met. A broader consequence the arbiter should see: under D3, nested arenas cannot have their own value, so transfer or endUse of one moves or ends both.",
      "suggested_fix": "Put this to arbitration: either relax D3's holder requirement for nested arenas, or reword the §5 case to 'release of the child's internal'. Until then, record the substituted scenario in report sections (d) and (g) as a deviation from the task case."
    },
    {
      "title": "reachable_base_owns_statics does not state that statics with an owning element stay owned by frame 0",
      "severity": "minor",
      "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:8139 (reachable_base_owns_statics)",
      "cause": "missing coverage",
      "evidence": "Brief step 1: `reachable_base_owns_nothing est réénoncé : le cadre 0 possède exactement les emplacements statiques et leur stockage possédé`. The new conclusion only says `pl.owner = .frame 0 ↔ q < statics.length ∧ (owning element) = none`, which is direct ownership. For a static whose encoding has an owning element, it says nothing. In Lean (rev10/stmt/checks3.lean) I took `stO := [((none,none,0),true), ((none,some 0,0),false)]` (ShapeOK holds, and S3.init gives owners [frame 0, place 0]). A state `tO` where static 1 is owned by `.place 2`, and place 2 by frame 1, satisfies all four conjuncts of the conclusion, yet `¬ OwnedByFrame tO.P 0 1` is provable. So the theorem does not exclude a static leaving frame 0's ownership, and the 'every static place is owned by frame 0' half of 'exactement' is unproven for owned statics. No pass-5 test uses an owned static either.",
      "suggested_fix": "Add the conjunct `∀ q < statics.length, OwnedByFrame s.P 0 q`, by proving an invariant that statics stay transitively owned by frame 0. Otherwise, list this direction as unproven in the report."
    },
    {
      "title": "ao2_rejected_at_depend now rules out reachability only from the empty static storage, though the same proof works for every static storage",
      "severity": "minor",
      "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:7870 (ao2_rejected_at_depend)",
      "cause": "formalization error",
      "evidence": "The statement changed from `¬ Reachable K0 ao2` to `¬ Reachable K0 [] ao2`, and likewise for `exitEff ao2`. With `S3.init statics`, 'ao2 is not reached' now means for every statics, not just []. The pass-4 meaning carries over at no cost: this builds in rev10/stmt/checks.lean: `example : ∀ statics, ¬ Reachable K0 statics ao2 := fun statics hr => absurd ((reachable_access_invariant_underDD (KT_dd [] [] [] [] []) hr).2.1.ao) (fun h => absurd (h 0 (by decide) 5 (by decide)) (by decide))`. Narrowing to [] is not forced by the brief. Brief (o) asks for such domain changes to be listed.",
      "suggested_fix": "Restate both negative conjuncts as `∀ statics, ¬ Reachable K0 statics _` (the helper `unr` already works for any statics), or list the narrowing in report section (o)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Dependency-only return case: the docstring gives the wrong indices, and the read-reject verdict would also hold before the call",
      "severity": "minor",
      "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:8474-8492 (dd0..dd3)",
      "cause": "formalization error",
      "evidence": "The docstring says 'the call passes 4, which observes the part 1, and 5, which modifies the result; the callee value 6 depends on 4 and is returned to 3'. `#eval dd1.A` gives [(none,[1,2],modify), (none,[3],modify), (some 0,[1],observe), (some 1,[3],modify), (none,[4],modify)] and `dd1.P.length = 5`. The definitions are `enterEff … [2, 3] …`, `dependEff … 4 2` and `transferEff dd2 4 3`. So the parameters are authorities 2 and 3, and the callee value is place 4, depending on authority 2. Separately, `Read3Step 1 [1] dd0 .reject` also builds (checks3.lean): authority 1 (root of place 3, footprint [3]) never covered leaf 1, so the reject verdict does not depend on the return scenario. Only the companion `decide` check (no active authority covering leaf 1 is held by place 3) carries the case's content.",
      "suggested_fix": "Fix the indices in the docstring (params 2 and 3, callee value 4, depends on 2). State that the verdict rests on the 'no authority held by 3' check, or move that fact into the verdict example."
    },
    {
      "title": "arenaInv_transport keeps a hypothesis conjunct it no longer uses, and its docstring still says 'owned root'",
      "severity": "minor",
      "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:6077 (arenaInv_transport)",
      "cause": "formalization error",
      "evidence": "`hA` still requires `(y.origin = none → y'.origin = none)`. Once ArenaInv dropped `y.origin = none` for internal, every destructuring in the proof discards that conjunct: `obtain ⟨yi', hyi', mi, fi, -, -, -⟩ := hA _ yi hyi`, `obtain ⟨y'', hy'', -, -, ha, -⟩ := hA x y hy` and `obtain ⟨y', hy', m', f', -, o', -⟩ := hA _ y hy`. The statement therefore carries an unjustified hypothesis (AGENTS.md: never add an unjustified hypothesis). The docstring still reads 'keep an origin equal to `internal` or absent; the storage stays an owned root', while the hypothesis is now `OwnedStorage`.",
      "suggested_fix": "Drop the unused conjunct from `hA` (and from callers), and update the docstring to 'storage owned by a place' and 'origin equal to internal'."
    }
  ]

# AGENTS.md

Claude Code implements. Codex reviews. Both follow this file.

## Source of truth

- `specs/` is normative and the only source of semantics. Before acting, read the spec text the task depends on. Never rely on memory, summaries, comments or earlier sessions.
- Never restate spec content in code comments or agent files. Point to its location.
- Spec beats code. If the spec is ambiguous, contradictory or silent on something the task needs: stop and report the exact passage with a concrete example of the problem. Never pick an interpretation yourself.
- Representation choices (structure or inductive type, function or relation) are yours when they change no accepted program and no behavior. A choice that does is a semantic question: stop and report.

## Scope

- Do exactly the task. No unrequested features, generalization, refactoring or "robustness" additions. Put suggestions in the report.
- Do not edit `specs/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `formal/DESIGN.md` unless the task says so.

## Lean

- The Lake project is in `formal/`. `formal/DESIGN.md` governs how to formalize, never what the semantics is. Propose design decisions it does not settle in your report; never take them silently.
- Every definition or theorem that encodes a spec rule cites the rule's location in its docstring.
- A definition says what its rule says. Never make a definition more permissive, add an unjustified hypothesis or narrow a theorem's domain to obtain a proof.
- Never change a theorem statement, or a definition it depends on, to make a proof go through. If stuck, stop and report the goal state.
- Never use `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom` or `native_decide`.
- Every `.lean` file under `formal/` is part of the build target.
- Done means:
  - `lake build` (in `formal/`) succeeds;
  - this prints nothing: `grep -rnE '\b(sorry|admit|native_decide)\b|^\s*axiom\b' --include='*.lean' --exclude-dir=.lake .`
  - for each theorem completed by the task, `#print axioms` lists nothing beyond `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.

## Report

Spec passages implemented (by location), what changed, what is unproven or open, spec problems found.

## Review (Codex)

Adversarial and read-only. For each change, check:

- It says exactly what the spec says: not stronger, not weaker. Read definitions, hypotheses and quantifiers, not only proofs. A theorem that holds because a definition is too permissive or its hypotheses are unsatisfiable is blocking.
- Each formalized rule cites its spec location.
- No theorem statement or dependency was changed without the task allowing it.
- No interpretation was chosen silently where the spec is unclear.
- Nothing outside the task was added.

When a milestone is declared complete, compare the rules in its announced scope with the spec locations cited in `formal/`, and list every rule left without a definition or theorem.

Every finding needs evidence: a spec quote, a counterexample or command output. No evidence, no finding. Never ask for additions beyond the task.

Output: verdict (block / changes / ok), then each finding with severity, location, cause (formalization error, missing coverage or spec defect) and evidence.
- [ERN formal exploratory passes](ern-formal-mm02-exploration.md) — French briefs, MM-02/MM-03 branches, reports/ never merged, spec in ~/Downloads, axiom rule, no-weakening diff
